title: Atari Anniversary Edition
text:
Atari Arcade Hits is a video game compilation of twelve Atari arcade games, developed by Digital Eclipse and published by Hasbro Interactive for Windows. It was originally released in two volumes, the first in July 1999, the second in 2000, respectively.

Following Hasbro Interactive's purchase by Infogrames in January 2001, the company's US publishing division Infogrames, Inc. released an updated version of the game entitled Atari Anniversary Edition in 2001, alongside ports to the Dreamcast, PlayStation (as Atari Anniversary Edition Redux) and Game Boy Advance (as Atari Anniversary Advance). However, the games and content slightly differ by platform.

Features
Atari Arcade Hits 1 and Atari Arcade Hits 2 feature twelve Atari arcade games, six each, from over the years in an arcade-based setting. In addition to the games, the player can also view bonus content, with both volumes containing box art and manuals for the games included, as well as promotional material and advertisements. The first volume also contains an aftermarket level replacement hack of Tempest titled "Tempest Tubes", and several interviews with Atari founder Nolan Bushnell. Atari Anniversary Edition includes all the content from both volumes with slight updates.

The Dreamcast and PlayStation ports retain the games and bonus content from the original; although the latter version swaps out Millipede and Crystal Castles for Black Widow and Space Duel, which weren't included on the original releases. The Game Boy Advance version includes the games from the first volume, but with Pong replaced with Battlezone from the second. The bonus content included with this version includes "Tempest Tubes" and an exclusive mode called "Trivia Challenge", which consists of questions about Atari and its 1980s video games.

Release
In 2000, Hasbro Interactive released Atari Greatest Hits, a re-release of both volumes packaged together as a 2-CD set., while Atari Anniversary Edition packages both volumes on a single disc.

Reception
Atari Arcade Hits
IGN gave the first volume an 8.6/10, with the reviewer praising the emulation quality of the games and bonus content.

Atari Anniversary Edition

The Atari Anniversary Edition version of the game received "mixed or average" reviews, while Atari Anniversary Advance received "generally favorable" reviews, according to the review aggregation website Metacritic.
